scope: Physical, ecological, traffic and selected economics bibliographic reconciliation. Metadata only; no equations, inputs, IDs, layout, connectors or time settings changed.

before.description: Models traffic density, speed, and congestion on highways. Based on Lighthill-Whitham-Richards (LWR) model. DOI: 10.1098/rspa.1955.0088
before.reference: Lighthill MJ, Whitham GB (1955). On Kinematic Waves II: A Theory of Traffic Flow on Long Crowded Roads. Proc. R. Soc. A.

after.description: Illustrative traffic stock-flow model using a linear speed-density relation and queue heuristics. Lighthill and Whitham (1955), Part II, is conceptual background; this file is not a verified spatial discretization or reproduction of the LWR conservation law. Parameter units, vehicle conservation and numerical stability require review.
after.reference: Lighthill, M.J. and Whitham, G.B. (1955). On kinematic waves II. A theory of traffic flow on long crowded roads. Proceedings of the Royal Society A 229(1178):317-345. doi:10.1098/rspa.1955.0089.

models.limitations: The cited source is a spatial conservation-law theory. The file uses lumped stocks and additional heuristic queues; no validation of discretization, boundary supply/demand, units, or solver stability was established.

before.description: Models urban traffic congestion and flow dynamics. Based on Lighthill-Whitham-Richards (LWR) theory and Vickrey bottleneck model for rush-hour dynamics. Reference: Highway Capacity Manual. Transportation Research Board. Source: https://www.trb.org/
before.reference: Lighthill MJ, Whitham GB. On kinematic waves II. A theory of traffic flow on long crowded roads. Proceedings of the Royal Society A. 1955;229(1178):317-345.

after.description: Illustrative traffic stock-flow model using a linear speed-density relation and queue heuristics. Lighthill and Whitham (1955), Part II, is conceptual background; this file is not a verified spatial discretization or reproduction of the LWR conservation law. Parameter units, vehicle conservation and numerical stability require review.
after.reference: Lighthill, M.J. and Whitham, G.B. (1955). On kinematic waves II. A theory of traffic flow on long crowded roads. Proceedings of the Royal Society A 229(1178):317-345. doi:10.1098/rspa.1955.0089.

models.limitations: The cited source is a spatial conservation-law theory. The file uses lumped stocks and additional heuristic queues; no validation of discretization, boundary supply/demand, units, or solver stability was established.

before.description: Fundamental traffic flow model relating speed, density, and flow. Source: Greenshields (1935), Highway Research Board.
before.reference: Greenshields, B.D. (1935). A Study of Traffic Capacity. Highway Research Board Proceedings 14:448-477.

after.description: Illustrative traffic stock-flow model using the Greenshields linear speed-density relation. Capacity follows from the parabolic flow-density relation. Arrival forcing and queue equations are local illustrative additions, not a reproduction of the 1935 empirical study; parameter calibration and numerical stability remain unverified.
after.reference: Greenshields, B.D. (1935). A Study of Traffic Capacity. Highway Research Board Proceedings 14, Part I:448-477 (including discussion).

models.limitations: TRB original and publisher catalogue identify the 1935 study. The former DOI identifies a different publication. Linear closure and its algebraic capacity can be checked independently; the queue and forcing are not source validated.

before.description: Model of eukaryotic cell cycle control. Shows cyclin-CDK interactions, checkpoints, and cell division control. Based on Tyson & Novak models. Nobel Prize 2001 research (Hartwell, Hunt, Nurse). Reference: Based on system dynamics methodology (Sterman, 2000; Forrester, 1961). Source: https://systemdynamics.org/
before.reference: Tyson & Novak (2001). Regulation of the eukaryotic cell cycle. Nobel Prize 2001 (Hartwell, Hunt, Nurse).

after.description: Illustrative cyclin-CDK and APC feedback model. Tyson and Novak (2001) provides conceptual background; this four-stock file is not a verified reproduction of a particular equation set in that paper. Checkpoint logic, mass-dependent synthesis, APC kinetics and continuous division loss are local assumptions requiring scientific review.
after.reference: Tyson, J.J. and Novak, B. (2001). Regulation of the eukaryotic cell cycle: molecular antagonism, hysteresis, and irreversible transitions. Journal of Theoretical Biology 210(2):249-263. doi:10.1006/jtbi.2001.2293.

models.limitations: Corrected DOI formerly identified Cats. Exact equation/table mapping and parameters have not been established; k3 and K3 (also k4/K4, k5/K5, k6/K6) must remain distinct symbols.

before.description: Model of wildfire spread through forest landscape. Shows fuel load, fire intensity, and spread rate dynamics. Based on Rothermel fire spread model and fire ecology research. Reference: NIFC National Interagency Fire Center. Source: https://www.nifc.gov/
before.reference: Rothermel, R.C. (1972). A mathematical model for predicting fire spread in wildland fuels. USDA Forest Service.

after.description: Illustrative forest fire stock-flow model with heuristic wind, fuel and humidity multipliers. Rothermel (1972) is background on surface fire spread; this file does not implement the published reaction-intensity, propagating-flux and heat-sink formulation. Area, perimeter and fuel units, depletion and calibration require review.
after.reference: Rothermel, R.C. (1972). A mathematical model for predicting fire spread in wildland fuels. USDA Forest Service Research Paper INT-115. 40 pp. doi:10.2737/INT-RP-115.

models.limitations: The original defines spread through a heat-source/heat-sink balance, not the local multiplier formula. No Rothermel fidelity is claimed.

before.description: Classic model of thermal convection in a fluid layer heated from below. Above a critical Rayleigh number, convection cells form. This is a fundamental paradigm for pattern formation in physics. Source: Bénard (1900), Rayleigh (1916). DOI: 10.1098/rspa.1916.0076
before.reference: Rayleigh, Lord (1916). On convection currents in a horizontal layer of fluid when the higher temperature is on the under side. Phil. Mag., 32, 529-546.

after.description: Illustrative heated-fluid-layer model using the dimensionless Rayleigh number and a heuristic convection-amplitude growth rule. Rayleigh (1916) is conceptual background, not the source of this stock-flow equation set. The threshold 1708 depends on boundary conditions; heat transport feedback, nonlinear saturation and calibrated units are not established.
after.reference: Rayleigh, Lord (1916). On convection currents in a horizontal layer of fluid, when the higher temperature is on the under side. Philosophical Magazine, Series 6, 32(192):529-546. doi:10.1080/14786441608635602.

models.limitations: The file has independent heating/cooling and unbounded amplitude growth, rather than a verified boundary-value stability calculation. No coefficient or equation edits were made.

before.description: Dynamic stochastic general equilibrium model with households, firms, and central bank. Workhorse of modern macroeconomics. Used by central banks for policy analysis. Reference: NBER Economic Research. Source: https://www.nber.org/
before.reference: Smets F, Wouters R. Shocks and Frictions in US Business Cycles: A Bayesian DSGE Approach. American Economic Review. 2007;97(3):586-606.

after.description: Illustrative three-variable New Keynesian adjustment model with exogenous expectations and an interest-rate rule. Smets and Wouters (2007) is conceptual background; this file is not their estimated stochastic DSGE model and does not reproduce its rational-expectations solution, seven shocks, frictions or fitted parameters.
after.reference: Smets, F. and Wouters, R. (2007). Shocks and Frictions in US Business Cycles: A Bayesian DSGE Approach. American Economic Review 97(3):586-606. doi:10.1257/aer.97.3.586.

models.limitations: The local continuous adjustment equations with fixed expectations are not the published stochastic rational-expectations system. DOI correction does not validate them.

before.description: Advanced system dynamics model of two-sided platform economics capturing network effects between users and providers, with competition and multi-homing dynamics. Reference: NBER Economic Research. Source: https://www.nber.org/
before.reference: Rysman (2009) based on Rochet & Tirole (2003). The Economics of Two-Sided Markets. Journal of Economic Perspectives, 23(3), 125-143.

after.description: Illustrative stock-flow model of users, providers, perceived value and platform switching. Rysman (2009) is conceptual background on cross-side network effects; the acquisition, churn, value and competition equations here are local assumptions, not a verified published quantitative model or calibrated forecast.
after.reference: Rysman, M. (2009). The Economics of Two-Sided Markets. Journal of Economic Perspectives 23(3):125-143. doi:10.1257/jep.23.3.125.

models.limitations: The paper is an overview. The local model does not establish pricing equilibria, explicit multihoming, empirical calibration, or nonnegative churn.

before.description: A predator-prey model incorporating the Allee effect - reduced fitness at low population densities. Shows how minimum viable population thresholds affect ecosystem stability. Reference: UN World Population Prospects. Source: https://population.un.org/
before.reference: Courchamp F, Clutton-Brock T, Grenfell B. Inverse density dependence and the Allee effect. Trends in Ecology & Evolution. 1999;14(10):405-410.

after.description: Illustrative predator-prey model with a weak Allee factor N/(A+N) and saturating predation. The factor reduces per-capita prey growth at low density but does not create an intrinsic positive extinction threshold. Courchamp et al. (1999) is conceptual review background; the local equations and parameters are not an exact reproduction.
after.reference: Courchamp, F., Clutton-Brock, T. and Grenfell, B. (1999). Inverse density dependence and the Allee effect. Trends in Ecology & Evolution 14(10):405-410. doi:10.1016/S0169-5347(99)01683-3.

models.limitations: For 0<N<K and zero predators, r*N/(A+N)*(1-N/K)>0: this is a weak Allee form, not a strong-Allee threshold. The symbols a and A must remain distinct.

before.description: A model of phosphorus dynamics in lakes demonstrating eutrophication processes. Based on the pioneering work of Vollenweider (1968) on lake nutrient loading and trophic state. Reference: Based on system dynamics methodology (Sterman, 2000; Forrester, 1961). Source: https://systemdynamics.org/
before.reference: Vollenweider RA. Scientific fundamentals of the eutrophication of lakes and flowing waters. OECD Technical Report, 1968.

after.description: Illustrative phosphorus-water, sediment and algae stock-flow model. Vollenweider (1968) is background on nutrient loading and trophic state; this file is not a verified reproduction of his loading model. Sediment release, anoxia feedback and algal kinetics are local assumptions; phosphorus uptake into algae and biomass stoichiometry are not represented.
after.reference: Vollenweider, R.A. (1968). Scientific fundamentals of the eutrophication of lakes and flowing waters, with particular reference to nitrogen and phosphorus as factors in eutrophication. OECD Technical Report DAS/CSI/68.27. Paris.

models.limitations: The old DOI identifies a pied-flycatcher study. EPA identifies the original report; Vollenweider authored the retrospective account. This is bibliographic recovery only, not a claim to have inspected the full original report.

before.description: A comprehensive model of the global carbon cycle including atmosphere, ocean, and terrestrial reservoirs. Models anthropogenic CO2 emissions, ocean uptake, and land-use change impacts. Reference: IPCC (2021). Climate Change 2021: The Physical Science Basis. Source: https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg1/
before.reference: Sarmiento JL, Gruber N. Ocean Biogeochemical Dynamics. Princeton University Press, 2006.

after.description: Illustrative global carbon reservoir stock-flow model. Sarmiento and Gruber (2006) is textbook background on ocean biogeochemistry; no particular chapter, equation set, calibrated parameter table or observational validation has been established for this file.
after.reference: Sarmiento, J.L. and Gruber, N. (2006). Ocean Biogeochemical Dynamics. Princeton University Press. doi:10.2307/j.ctt3fgxqx.

models.limitations: Replaces an article DOI with the named textbook. Reservoir exchange equations and parameter provenance remain unverified.

before.description: A simplified four-box model of the global carbon cycle showing exchanges between atmosphere, ocean surface, deep ocean, and terrestrial biosphere. Based on Sarmiento & Gruber (2006) and IPCC AR5 carbon cycle. Reference: IPCC (2021). Climate Change 2021: The Physical Science Basis. Cambridge University Press. Source: https://www.ipcc.ch/
before.reference: Sarmiento JL, Gruber N. Ocean Biogeochemical Dynamics. Princeton University Press, 2006.

after.description: Illustrative global carbon reservoir stock-flow model. Sarmiento and Gruber (2006) is textbook background on ocean biogeochemistry; no particular chapter, equation set, calibrated parameter table or observational validation has been established for this file.
after.reference: Sarmiento, J.L. and Gruber, N. (2006). Ocean Biogeochemical Dynamics. Princeton University Press. doi:10.2307/j.ctt3fgxqx.

models.limitations: Replaces an article DOI with the named textbook. Reservoir exchange equations and parameter provenance remain unverified.

before.description: Model of ocean carbonate chemistry showing how CO2 absorption changes pH and affects marine calcifiers. Based on Zeebe & Wolf-Gladrow (2001) carbonate chemistry and Orr et al. (2005) projections. Reference: Based on project dynamics models (Lyneis & Ford, 2007). Source: https://systemdynamics.org/
before.reference: Zeebe RE, Wolf-Gladrow D. CO2 in Seawater: Equilibrium, Kinetics, Isotopes. Elsevier, 2001.

after.description: Illustrative ocean carbon and acidification stock-flow model. Zeebe and Wolf-Gladrow (2001) is textbook background; an equation-by-equation match to the carbonate equilibrium, alkalinity, pH scales and kinetic system has not been established. Parameters and acidification outputs remain unvalidated.
after.reference: Zeebe, R.E. and Wolf-Gladrow, D.A. (2001). CO2 in Seawater: Equilibrium, Kinetics, Isotopes. Elsevier Oceanography Series 65. Amsterdam: Elsevier.

models.limitations: The old DOI describes clay weathering. The author bibliography confirms the named textbook; the replacement is a bibliography URL, not an asserted equation source.

before.description: Classic chemical oscillation model demonstrating self-organizing patterns. Oregonator model variant. Source: Field & Noyes (1974), JCP. Nobel Prize 1977 (Prigogine).
before.reference: Field, R.J. & Noyes, R.M. (1974). Oscillations in chemical systems. IV. J Chem Phys 60:1877-1884.

after.description: Illustrative three-intermediate chemical kinetics variant inspired by the Oregonator. Field and Noyes (1974) is the original source, but the local effective coefficients, concentrations and time units have not been mapped to its reaction scheme. Stiffness and numerical stability at the supplied defaults remain unresolved; oscillatory behavior is not validated.
after.reference: Field, R.J. and Noyes, R.M. (1974). Oscillations in chemical systems. IV. Limit cycle behavior in a model of a real chemical reaction. Journal of Chemical Physics 60(5):1877-1884. doi:10.1063/1.1681288.

models.limitations: The first X derivative is -2001986 at X=1,Y=2,Z=1; Euler dt=.01 overshoots below zero. No arbitrary coefficient rescaling or silent replacement was made.

before.description: Models the Belousov-Zhabotinsky oscillating chemical reaction, a classic example of chemical pattern formation
before.reference: Field, R.J. & Noyes, R.M. (1974) Oscillations in chemical systems. J. Chem. Phys. 60:1877

after.description: Incomplete Oregonator teaching scaffold. Field and Noyes (1974) is the original chemical-oscillator reference. This file contains three stocks and epsilon, q and f inputs but no flows or stock derivative equations, so it does not implement the published Oregonator or demonstrate chemical oscillations.
after.reference: Field, R.J. and Noyes, R.M. (1974). Oscillations in chemical systems. IV. Limit cycle behavior in a model of a real chemical reaction. Journal of Chemical Physics 60(5):1877-1884. doi:10.1063/1.1681288.

models.limitations: The old DOI identifies coil-stretch physics. The current file has no kinetic equations; reconstructing a dimensioned or nondimensionalized Oregonator would require a deliberate specification and parameter mapping, not a citation swap.

before.description: Labor market frictions create unemployment even in equilibrium. Workers search for jobs, firms post vacancies, matching creates surplus divided by bargaining. Nobel Prize 2010. Reference: BLS Employment Situation. Source: https://www.bls.gov/
before.reference: Mortensen DT, Pissarides CA. Job Creation and Job Destruction in the Theory of Unemployment. Review of Economic Studies. 1994;61(3):397-415. Nobel Prize 2010.

after.description: Illustrative labor-market search and matching stock-flow model. Mortensen and Pissarides (1994) is conceptual background; the job-specific shock process, endogenous destruction threshold, wage bargaining and equilibrium conditions of that paper have not been mapped to this file. Local equations and parameters are unverified.
after.reference: Mortensen, D.T. and Pissarides, C.A. (1994). Job Creation and Job Destruction in the Theory of Unemployment. Review of Economic Studies 61(3):397-415. doi:10.2307/2297896.

models.limitations: Corrected an unrelated DOI to the named original work. Conceptual or empirical background only; quantitative equation and parameter provenance remains unverified.

before.description: A model of startup ecosystem dynamics including funding cycles, success rates, and ecosystem feedback effects. Reference: Blank, S. (2013). The Four Steps to the Epiphany. K&S Ranch. Source: https://steveblank.com/
before.reference: Feld B. Startup Communities: Building an Entrepreneurial Ecosystem in Your City. Wiley, 2012.

after.description: Illustrative startup ecosystem stock-flow model. Feld (2012) provides qualitative background on entrepreneurial communities; its quantitative startup, funding, talent and feedback equations are local assumptions without an established published equation set or calibration.
after.reference: Feld, B. (2012). Startup Communities: Building an Entrepreneurial Ecosystem in Your City. Wiley. doi:10.1002/9781119204459.

models.limitations: Corrected an unrelated DOI to the named original work. Conceptual or empirical background only; quantitative equation and parameter provenance remains unverified.

before.description: Models the dynamics of semiconductor chip shortages, including fab capacity constraints, demand amplification, inventory dynamics, and the bullwhip effect in the automotive and electronics industries. Based on analysis of the 2020-2023 global chip shortage.
before.reference: Attinasi MG, et al. The semiconductor shortage and its implication for euro area trade and industrial production. ECB Economic Bulletin. 2021. Semiconductor Industry Association reports.

after.description: Illustrative semiconductor supply-chain stock-flow model. Attinasi et al. (2021) is empirical background on shortages, trade and production; the capacity, inventory, backlog and adjustment equations here are local assumptions, not an ECB forecasting model or a verified replication.
after.reference: Attinasi, M.G., De Stefani, R., Frohm, E., Gunnella, V., Koester, G., Melemenidis, A. and Toth, M. (2021). The semiconductor shortage and its implication for euro area trade, production and prices. ECB Economic Bulletin, Issue 4/2021, Box 6.

models.limitations: Corrected an unrelated DOI to the named original work. Conceptual or empirical background only; quantitative equation and parameter provenance remains unverified.

unresolved: These corrections do not establish scientific fidelity or repair failing numerical defaults. See per-model limitations.
